Next year's iPhone Pro models are expected to feature a brand-new all-glass design, coinciding with the 20th anniversary of the iPhone. New leaks today reveal Apple's progress on this innovative model.

Here's the latest on Apple's unique iPhone 20 Pro design

The innovative iPhone Ultra is on the horizon, which will be Apple's first-ever foldable phone. But next year will bring another unique all-new iPhone design.

Rumors suggest Apple is working on a special all-glass design for next year's iPhone Pro models. The new device is reportedly set to feature a larger screen with a quad-curved display, where the glass extends to the edges of the body, creating a visually bezel-less effect.

Weibo leaker Fixed Focus Digital today updated on Apple's progress in achieving this unique look in a new post.

He says the company is using the same glass assembly process as the iPhone Air, but with adjustments to accommodate more rounded materials.

The post also mentions improvements in two areas:

  • Thermal performance
  • Body thickness

It's still too early to know what thickness and design materials Apple is aiming for. But signs so far indicate this new model will draw inspiration from both the iPhone Air and Ultra, but won't prioritize slimness in the same way.

Based on these latest updates, it sounds like we could see a model that combines the design innovations of the iPhone Air and Ultra, while retaining the performance and battery life that Pro users expect.

Pro users don't want slimness prioritized. But if Apple can deliver a comparable experience in a slightly slimmer body, paired with a unique all-glass look, that would be very appealing.

How interested are you in next year's rumored iPhone Pro 20 model? Let us know in the comments.
